settings.title: Settings
settings.help: All settings apply without a restart; each one says when a change takes effect. ● — differs from the default, ↺ — restore the default.
settings.unsavedLeave: Unsaved settings changes will be lost. Leave anyway?
settings.applyText_one: Some changes affect only new connections. Reconnect {{count}} miner now? It disconnects and comes right back.
settings.applyText_other: Some changes affect only new connections. Reconnect {{count}} miners now? They disconnect gradually and come right back.

test_worker.title: Test worker
test_worker.desc: Worker name used by background checks, the Test button and checks before a switch. Checks authorize and wait for a job. This worker may stay in the pool dashboard as inactive.

switch_drain.title: Reconnect window
switch_drain.desc: How long the proxy spreads out disconnecting miners on a pool switch, failover, failback and “Reconnect all”. Longer is gentler on the pool, but part of the farm stays on the old pool longer. 0 means all at once.

failback_delay.title: Failback delay
failback_delay.desc: How long the active pool must stay healthy before miners return to it from a fallback pool. Prevents flapping when the pool is unstable.

pool_probe_interval.title: Pool check interval
pool_probe_interval.desc: How often the proxy checks every pool address: connection, mining.subscribe, authorization with the test worker and a mining.notify job, within 10 seconds. Two failed checks exclude an address; two successful checks confirm recovery.

tls_handshake_timeout.title: TLS handshake timeout
tls_handshake_timeout.desc: How long to wait for an ASIC to finish the TLS handshake on the TLS port before closing the connection.

first_message_timeout.title: First message timeout
first_message_timeout.desc: How long to wait for the first Stratum message after an ASIC connects. Protects against connections that send nothing. The proxy connects to the pool only after this message.

upstream_dial_timeout.title: Pool connect timeout
upstream_dial_timeout.desc: How long to wait for a connection (and TLS handshake) to one pool address before trying the next address or a fallback pool.

upstream_connect_budget.title: Total pool search time
upstream_connect_budget.desc: How long a session may try addresses and pools in total. If none answers, the ASIC connection is closed and the ASIC reconnects by itself.

miner_idle_timeout.title: ASIC idle timeout
miner_idle_timeout.desc: If an ASIC sends nothing for longer than this, the session is closed.

upstream_idle_timeout.title: Pool idle timeout
upstream_idle_timeout.desc: If the pool sends nothing for longer than this, the session is closed and the ASIC reconnects. Too small a value breaks sessions on pools that rarely send jobs.

upstream_job_timeout.title: Pool job timeout
upstream_job_timeout.desc: After authorization, how long to wait for a usable mining.notify job. Other messages do not extend this time. A timeout excludes the pool address and reconnects its miners through another address or a fallback pool. Must not exceed the pool idle timeout. Applies to open sessions immediately.

max_connections.title: Total connections
max_connections.desc: How many ASIC connections the proxy holds at once (TCP and TLS together). Extra ones are closed right away. Lowering the value does not disconnect miners already connected.

max_pending_connections.title: Connections awaiting first message
max_pending_connections.desc: How many connections may wait for their first Stratum message at the same time. Protects against slow-connection attacks.

max_conn_per_ip.title: Connections per IP
max_conn_per_ip.desc: Limit of connections from one address; 0 turns it off. ⚠ A whole farm usually reaches the internet from one IP: if you enable it, set it well above the number of ASICs.

max_line_bytes.title: Maximum message size
max_line_bytes.desc: If a single Stratum message (from an ASIC or a pool) is longer, the session is closed. Rarely needs changing.

tls_min_version.title: Minimum TLS version
tls_min_version.desc: The oldest TLS version the TLS port accepts. Lower it only if an old firmware cannot connect otherwise: 1.0 and 1.1 are insecure.

log_level.title: Log level
log_level.desc: How detailed the container logs are. debug is for troubleshooting: details of every session, the log volume grows a lot. Passwords are never logged at any level.

history_detail_retention.title: Detailed history
history_detail_retention.desc: How long per-minute statistics are kept. Charts for up to 3 days are drawn from them; longer periods use hourly points. Takes about 0.3–0.5 MB per day with a few pools.

history_retention.title: History retention
history_retention.desc: How long hourly statistics are kept for long-range charts. Takes about 10 KB per day, so years of history fit easily.

profit_switch.title: Profit switching
profit_switch.desc: On schedule the proxy compares the coins of the pools marked “Take part in profit switching”: network difficulty, block reward with fees and price, 24-hour averages from WhatToMine. Advise only shows what earns more; Auto makes the most profitable pool active, with the same pool check as a manual switch. An active pool that does not take part is left alone.

profit_interval.title: Profitability check interval
profit_interval.desc: How often to compare the coins and decide. More often reacts sooner to difficulty and price changes, but miners reconnect more often, and on PPLNS pools frequent switching loses income.

profit_margin.title: Switching margin
profit_margin.desc: How much more another coin must earn than the current one to switch to it. Protects against switching on noise: BTC and BCH usually differ by only 1–3%.

history_miner_retention.title: Miner history
history_miner_retention.desc: How long the hourly statistics of every miner (hashrate, shares, time online) are kept. The detailed history also has ten-minute points. Grows with the farm: about 1.3 KB a day per miner hourly and 8 KB detailed.

audit_retention.title: Audit log retention
audit_retention.desc: How long the audit log (who changed what, sign-ins, device decisions) is kept. Entries older than this are deleted together with their monthly file. A year or more is recommended: disputes are looked into with this log.

timed_switch.title: Timed switching
timed_switch.desc: At the start of every period the farm moves to the pool marked “Switch to this pool on the timer” in the pool editor, for example a solo pool, and after the set time returns to the pool and fallback order it had before. Every switch reconnects all miners within the reconnect window. If the timer pool fails its check, the farm stays where it is until the next period. A pool chosen by hand during that time stays.

timed_period.title: Timer period
timed_period.desc: How often the farm moves to the timer pool. The time on it starts at multiples of the period: every 30 minutes means at :00 and :30. “Start now” on the Dashboard starts a period at that moment, and the next ones follow from it.

timed_duration.title: Time on the timer pool
timed_duration.desc: How long the farm mines on the timer pool in every period; shorter than the period. 10 minutes every 30 minutes is a third of the hashrate.

offline_after.title: No shares for
offline_after.desc: An ASIC that has sent no shares for this long is offline: the event goes to Events and, with the Telegram bot set up, to the chats. A working ASIC sends a share every few seconds, so a minute tells an outage from a pause. An ASIC that shares rarely (low hashrate or a high share difficulty) gets 20 of its usual intervals between shares instead. For 5 minutes after the proxy starts nobody is reported: ASICs are reconnecting. ASICs are told apart by the worker name, so give every ASIC its own.

telegram_chats.title: Telegram chats
telegram_chats.desc: Ids of the chats that get the alerts and may use the bot commands (/status, /miners), comma-separated. To learn the id, send /start to the bot from the chat (add the bot to a group first): a chat that is not on the list gets its id in the answer. Group ids start with a minus.
telegram_chats.note: digits, a leading minus and commas, no spaces

telegram_language.title: Telegram language
telegram_language.desc: The language of the alerts and the bot answers.

hunt_switch.title: Block hunting
hunt_switch.desc: The farm goes to the XEC solo pool (a pool with coin XEC marked Solo pool) while an eCash block is no harder than usual, and returns to where it was as soon as anyone finds a block, the farm or someone else. Right after a block eCash wants one hundreds of times harder (Real Time Targeting), about two minutes later a usual one; after that the difficulty does not fall until the next block, so there is nothing to wait for. Every eCash block, about every 10 minutes, costs two reconnects of the farm. Works along with the timer and profit switching: the timer comes first, and profit switching picks the pool the farm returns to. The proxy has to be connected to the eCash pool to see blocks as they arrive.

profit_return_margin.title: Return margin
profit_return_margin.desc: With a main pool chosen below: once the coin the farm moved to earns less than this much more than the main pool's coin, the farm goes back to the main pool and stays there until another coin is ahead by the switching margin again. The gap between the two margins keeps the farm from bouncing between coins on small changes.

device_control.title: Device control
device_control.desc: On: only the customers and devices of the Customers section may mine. An unknown worker is recorded as pending and mines only after an administrator approves it; suspended, blocked and revoked devices are refused and cut off at once. Off: the proxy accepts any miner, as before.

device_auth_timeout.title: Login timeout
device_auth_timeout.desc: How long a connection may stay open without a login that device control accepted. Connections that only subscribe and never log in are closed after this time.

device_pending_limit.title: Devices awaiting approval per customer
device_pending_limit.desc: A customer may have this many devices waiting for approval. Logins of further unknown workers are refused and no record is made, so a leaked key cannot fill the list.

operator_share.title: Operator share
operator_share.desc: On: a customer's shares may be credited to the operator's own worker for part of the mining time. It happens only for a customer who gave consent, on a pool marked as crediting a second worker, with device control on. Off: every share goes to the customer, as before.

operator_share_kind.title: Kind of share
operator_share_kind.desc: Percent of the mining time, or minutes of mining per day spread over the cycles. One rule applies, never both.

operator_share_amount.title: Amount
operator_share_amount.desc: The percent, or the minutes per day, depending on the kind. For example 2 percent, or 60 minutes per day (about 4.17 percent).

operator_share_max_percent.title: Cap
operator_share_max_percent.desc: Whatever the amount says, the operator never takes more than this part of a customer's mining time, so a typo cannot take half of it.

operator_share_cycle.title: Cycle length
operator_share_cycle.desc: The operator's window of a device sits once in every cycle. A short cycle spreads the share evenly; a long one makes fewer, longer switches.

server.title: Server
server.help: Read only. These values are set in .env on the server and apply after docker compose up -d: changing a port from the UI would break Docker port publishing, and a mistake in the password would lock you out.

telegram.noChats: none: add a chat id above
telegram.help: Alerts come to the chats at most once a minute, collected into one message. An ASIC that comes back before the message is sent is left out, and one that keeps dropping out is reported at most every 15 minutes. Every change is in Events.
telegram.setup: Paste the bot token above to get alerts in Telegram. Without it the alerts go to Events only.
telegram.tokenReplace: set; paste a new one to replace it
telegram.tokenHelp: Better: set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in .env, so the token never passes through the browser. A token pasted here is checked with Telegram, kept in state.json on the server and never shown again.
telegram.removeText: The bot stops answering and alerts go to Events only. The chats stay in the settings.
telegram.tokenFromEnv: The bot token is set by TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in .env. Change it there and restart the container.

profit.title: Coin profitability
profit.farm: The farm at its current hashrate earns about {{revenue}} a day on {{coin}}, before pool fees.
profit.source: 24-hour averages of network difficulty, block reward (with fees) and price, before pool fees. Data:

decision.no_candidates: No pool takes part in profit switching: mark pools in the pool editor.
decision.manual: The active pool {{pool}} does not take part in profit switching, so it is left alone.
decision.best: {{coin}} earns the most of the coins of the pools taking part: staying.

decision.recommend: {{best}} earns {{adv}} more than {{coin}}: switching to {{pool}} is worth it.

devices.title: Customers and devices
devices.controlOff: Device control is off: every device may mine and none of the states below is enforced. Turn it on in Settings.
devices.pendingHelp: A new device is recorded the first time it connects. It cannot mine until you approve it, and you choose for how long.

actionHelp.approve: The device starts mining at once. Choose how long it may work.
actionHelp.reject: The device stays on record and is refused. You can reopen it later.
actionHelp.reopen: Moves the rejected device back to waiting for approval.
actionHelp.suspend: Pauses the device: its connections close now and it is refused until you enable it again.
actionHelp.resume: The device works again. Choose how long it may work from now on.
actionHelp.block: Cuts the device off: its connections close now and every reconnect is refused. Other devices of the customer are not touched. Allow restores its earlier state.
actionHelp.unblock: Restores the state the device had before it was blocked.
actionHelp.revoke: Takes access away for good. The record stays, so the same name cannot simply register again; deleting the record is the only way back.

expiry.label: How long it may work
expiry.noEndHelp: No end: it works until you disable or block it.
expiry.fromNow: A choice such as 1 month is counted from now.

error.invalid: Enter a valid date and time.
error.past: The end must be in the future.

devices.countInvalid: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
devices.connectionsHelp: How many live connections the device may have. 0 means one: a reconnecting ASIC replaces the old connection.
devices.slugHelp: 3–32 characters: lowercase letters, digits, _ and -. The ASIC logs in as name.worker.
devices.slugFixed: It cannot be changed: the ASICs log in with it.
devices.accountHelp: The customer's own account at the pool (for ViaBTC, the account name). The pool password is never asked for or kept.
devices.maxDevicesHelp: How many devices may be active or disabled at once. 0 is no limit.
devices.maxConnectionsHelp: How many live connections the customer may have. 0 is no limit.
devices.languageHelp: Language for messages to this customer.
devices.keyHelp: Give this key to the customer: the ASIC sends it as the password.
devices.keyLogin: The ASIC logs in as {{slug}}.<worker> with this key as the password.
devices.keyOnce: It is shown only now and is not kept. If it is lost, make a new key; the old one stops working then.
devices.customerStateHelp: Disabling or blocking a customer stops all of their devices at once; their records stay.
devices.consentHelp: Record that the customer agreed to the operator's share of their mining. Without this record nothing is ever taken from their mining.
devices.consentNoteHelp: For example where the signed agreement is kept.
devices.deleteDeviceBody: The record is removed. If this worker connects again it is a new device waiting for approval.
devices.newKeyBody: The old key stops working at once: the customer's ASICs must be changed to the new one.
devices.deleteCustomerBody: Only a customer without devices can be deleted.
